preconditions.expression: all(1 <= int(line.split()[0]) <= 10**5 for line in stdin.splitlines()[0:1]) and all(1 <= int(line.split()[1]) <= 4 for line in stdin.splitlines()[0:1])
preconditions.description: The first line contains two integers n (1 ≤ n ≤ 10^5) and k (1 ≤ k ≤ 4), representing the number of problems and teams, respectively.

preconditions.expression: len(stdin.splitlines()) == n + 1 and all(len(line.split()) == k for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:])
preconditions.description: There are exactly n lines after the first line, each containing k integers (0 or 1), where the j-th integer in the i-th line indicates whether the j-th team knows the i-th problem.

preconditions.expression: all(all(int(x) in {0, 1} for x in line.split()) for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:])
preconditions.description: Each of the k integers in every problem line is either 0 or 1.

postconditions.expression: stdout.strip().upper() == 'YES' if any(all(sum(int(problem[j] for problem in selected_problems)) <= len(selected_problems) // 2 for j in range(k)) for selected_problems in non_empty_subsets) else stdout.strip().upper() == 'NO'
postconditions.description: The output is 'YES' if and only if there exists a non-empty subset of problems (selected_problems) such that for every team j, the number of problems in the subset that team j knows is at most half the size of the subset. Here, non_empty_subsets is the set of all non-empty subsets of the n problems, and selected_problems is a list of problem lines (each line is a string of k 0/1 values).
